themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: AMD guided Q4 revenue to about $17 billion, plus or minus 3%, against about $16.2 to $16.3 billion expected, after Q3 revenue of $13.38 billion, up 45%; it sees data center sales up about 50% from Q3 (Nov 3). The FT and Reuters report Oracle cancelled a five year, roughly $7 billion lease of about 100,000 AI chips to Tencent in Southeast Asia after US officials raised concerns (Nov 4).
themes.for_you: No action. AMD is 'Accumulate on pullback' and closed at 483.90 on Nov 3 (Massive); do not chase a post report gap. The Oracle news shuts an offshore leasing route for Chinese buyers, a small hit to ORCL's backlog. NVDA is left out of both lists: China demand shifts, but US demand is unchanged.

themes.name: AI power and the grid
themes.what: After Democrats won both chambers, the Invesco Solar ETF (TAN) rose more than 8% before the open on Nov 4 on hopes for renewed clean energy tax credits (Yahoo). On Nov 3 GEV rose 6.49% to 918.20 and ENPH 8.92% to 30.42 (Massive). A Caterpillar director bought about $620,000 at $620.39 on Nov 2, filed Nov 3 (dashboard).
themes.for_you: No action. New tax credits need a law the President would sign, so this is a hope, not a policy. CAT is Wait; GEV has no setup. No puts on solar names after a one day jump.

themes.name: Defense, drones and reshoring
themes.what: Democrats won control of the House and Senate on Nov 3 (CBS, CNN), so a Democratic Congress will set defense budgets and oversight from January while the President keeps his veto. Defense names lagged before the open on Nov 4 (CNBC). Two Boeing directors bought about $1.5 million of stock near $172 on Oct 30, filed Nov 3 (dashboard).
themes.for_you: No action. LMT, RTX and GD stay 'Accumulate on pullback'; no puts on defense this week. NOC is marked bearish because analysts named it the most exposed to new program delays (24/7 Wall St, Oct 20). BA is rated Avoid; the director buys are worth noting but do not change that.

themes.name: Healthcare and Medtech: Aging, Heart, Sugar, Hearing, Sight
themes.what: Insulet's Q3 revenue was $842.0 million, up 19.2% and above its own guidance range; international Omnipod grew 31.7% and US Omnipod 14.7%; adjusted EPS rose 59.9% to $1.99 and adjusted operating margin rose 4.9 points to 22.0% (Insulet, Nov 4).
themes.for_you: No action. PODD is 'Accumulate on pullback' at 154.86 on Nov 3 (Massive); a beat is not a reason to chase. Wait for a pullback toward the zone or a dashboard setup with volume.

innovations.name: Financials
innovations.what: Daily rotation recheck. Upstart's Q3 originations rose 44% to $4.1 billion but slipped from Q2's $4.2 billion, and the CEO said the economy weighs on the near term outlook, though net income was $36.6 million (SEC 8-K, Nov 3). NiCE's Q3 AI recurring revenue grew 46% to $392 million while total revenue grew 8.0%, and it raised full year EPS guidance (Nov 4). DTCC's October tokenization launch is still not confirmed.
innovations.for_you: Long term: NICE is 'Buy zone now' (106.27 on Nov 3, zone 101.97 to 114.23); wait for the first close after today's report. UPST is left out of both lists: profits are up but volume slipped and the CEO sounded cautious; UPST closed at 21.37 on Nov 3 (Massive) and has no verdict.

countries.name: China
countries.what: Oracle cancelled a roughly $7 billion, five year lease of about 100,000 AI chips to Tencent in Southeast Asian data centers after US officials raised concerns, the FT and Reuters report (Nov 4). Guangdong officials had also urged Tencent to back Chinese made chips.
countries.for_you: No action. Offshore leasing was the way Chinese firms reached top US chips; this shows the US will close it. BABA is left out of both lists: it still has leasing deals, but the same pressure could reach them.

countries.name: Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran risk)
countries.what: Asked whether he would strike Iran after the midterms, Trump said 'No', adding 'We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it' (Bloomberg, Ynet). Reports had said strike plans were ready from as early as Nov 4 (CBS). Qatar says both sides are reviewing its proposal; Iran called the US reply 'not convincing'. Brent fell 1.44% to $102.11 by 11:55 GMT Nov 4 (Dow Jones).
countries.for_you: Swing: oil swings are about stops now. XOM 177.46 and CVX 225.27 on Nov 3 (Massive); keep stops at least at the 169.99 and 218.23 entries. FRO is left out of both lists: fewer strikes lowers the war premium, but Hormuz is still mostly shut.
